h1:
9 Budget Stays
on Koh Chang, Trat
We've Already Reviewed
heroSub: 9 hand-picked budget stays on Koh Chang that we've reviewed in depth — a boutique resort in a garden with a saltwater pool, hillside bungalows with a treehouse restaurant, a seafront guesthouse with sunset views, and an eco-resort with its own dive centre. Prices from around ฿550–900/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest take from real reviews for every stay
introH2: 🏝️ What kinds of budget stays are there on Koh Chang, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: "Budget stay" on Koh Chang doesn't mean one single thing, and that's exactly why choosing a cheap place here takes a bit of understanding before you book — some are boutique resorts tucked into quiet gardens with a saltwater pool, some are bungalows on a forested hillside with a treehouse restaurant and an infinity pool, some are guesthouses on the rocks selling sunset views for under a thousand baht, and some are eco-resorts with their own dive centre. · The thing travellers most often get wrong is that most budget stays on Koh Chang are not on the sand — they're usually set in gardens, up on the hills, or along the rocks, with a walk or a ride to reach the beach. Anyone who pays and expects a resort that opens straight onto the sand tends to feel let down. · This article rounds up 9 budget stays on Koh Chang that we've already reviewed in depth — across Hat Sai Khao (White Sand Beach), Kai Bae–Klong Prao, Bailan Bay, Lonely Beach and Bang Bao. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, lays out both the good and the honest caveats, compares prices across 3 sites, and includes direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Koh Chang has no train system and getting around the island is fairly limited — most people use the red songthaews that loop the island or rent a motorbike. · Reaching the island means taking a ferry across from the piers on the Trat mainland (Ao Thammachat / Centerpoint, near Laem Ngop), around 30–45 min, then carrying on down to the island's west coast. · The areas covered in this article: White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao) — the island's liveliest beach, packed with restaurants and bars · Klong Prao–Kai Bae Beach — mid-island, handy location, a long swimmable sandy beach, lovely sunsets · Bailan Bay — a small, quiet bay along the rocks, good for snorkelling · Lonely Beach (Hat Sai Yao) — the backpacker and beach-bar crowd · Bang Bao — at the far south of the island, an old fishing village, quiet, good for divers · Almost everywhere, renting a motorbike is recommended for getting around easily.

entries.name: Macura Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near White Sand Beach · ~5 min drive to the beach
entries.addr: 36/4 Moo 4, Ko Chang, Ko Chang District, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among the 9 budget stays we reviewed, if you go purely by score, Macura Resort is the highest at 9.0 on Trip.com (Agoda 8.6 · Booking 8.8). · It's a small boutique resort of around 16 units set in a shady green garden full of mature trees and tropical flowers, open since 2010 and run by Thai-European owners who come down to welcome and look after guests themselves — which is why so many reviews use the phrase "like staying at a friend's house." · The thing it gets talked about most for is the saltwater swimming pool in the middle of the garden, which real reviews say is easy to swim in, doesn't sting your eyes and has no harsh chlorine smell, paired with a pool bar where you can sip coffee in the morning and a cold beer in the evening. · There are several room types, from the garden-view Deluxe Bungalow and pool-view Superior to the highlight Deluxe Tree House raised on stilts in the garden. · The thing to understand before booking — and reviews say the same — is that this is not a beachfront resort; it's a garden stay set back from the beach, around a 5-minute drive or motorbike ride to White Sand Beach, the island's liveliest, so come with transport sorted. · Honest caveats from the reviews: pool upkeep and some parts of the resort can be inconsistent at times, a few of the bamboo rooms don't block sound well, and food options on site are limited. · Best for couples, travellers who like peace and quiet, and small families who value a pretty garden, a saltwater pool and personal care more than a beachfront location — at a starting price of just a few hundred baht.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want the most quiet and the best room condition, ask for a pool-view Superior or a concrete bungalow rather than the bamboo rooms, which don't block sound well. · Check whether breakfast is charged separately or included in the room rate, and if you're not driving yourself, ask about pier pick-up in advance.
pros: Highest score in the set at 9.0 · a quiet, private garden made for proper relaxing
Saltwater pool, easy to swim in without stinging your eyes (the thing reviews praise most)
Thai-European owners give a warm welcome and look after guests themselves, helping arrange tours
From just ฿700/night, excellent value for this kind of setting
cons: Not on the beach — you'll need transport for the ~5-minute ride to White Sand Beach
Pool upkeep and some parts of the resort can be inconsistent at times (from reviews)
Some bamboo rooms don't block sound well · on-site food options are limited

entries.name: Oasis Koh Chang
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the hill above Lonely Beach · 3 min walk down to the village
tags: 🌴 Bungalows in the forest on the hill
entries.addr: 4/28 Moo 1, Lonely Beach, Koh Chang Tai, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among these 9 stays, if you go by sheer character, Oasis Koh Chang is the one people talk about most — a small bungalow resort of around 17 units hidden on the hill above Lonely Beach village, on the side near Kai Bae Beach. · What sets it apart from other bungalows at the same price is its restaurant with a treehouse pavilion — a multi-level timber deck raised high above the dining house, with panoramic views over forest, sea and islands, which many reviews call one of the best sunset-watching spots in the area, paired with an infinity pool whose edge looks like it runs straight into the treetops, which reviews say is "prettier and cleaner than the price suggests." · Rooms split into the original timber fan bungalows, the cheapest option, and newer A/C rooms like the Deluxe Studio/Bungalow, which reviews say are great value at the mid-range level. · Food is another plus — generous Thai-Western portions, consistent in quality. · The thing to understand before booking: this is not a beachfront stay; it's around a 3-minute walk down to Lonely Beach village and 7–10 minutes down to the beach, with an uphill climb on the way back. · Honest caveats: some of the older timber bungalows are starting to show wear, fan rooms get hot in the hot season, and long-tailed macaques drop by regularly since it borders the national park forest — keep food well sealed. · Best for backpackers, laid-back couples, and anyone who values atmosphere and value over sleeping right on the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Order a cold drink and climb up to the treehouse pavilion at sunset — that's the highlight you shouldn't miss. · If you want comfort and cool air, especially in the hot season, choose the newer A/C rooms (Deluxe Studio/Bungalow) over the older timber fan bungalows, and rent a motorbike for going up and down the hill.
pros: Treehouse restaurant — a sunset spot with tasty food in generous portions
Infinity pool with forest-sea views, prettier and cleaner than the price suggests
Newer A/C rooms are great value, friendly staff who look after you closely
From just ฿900/night, the best value among the budget bungalows
cons: Not on the beach — set on the hill, around a 10-minute walk down, uphill on the way back
Some of the older timber bungalows are starting to show wear · fan rooms get hot in the hot season
Long-tailed macaques drop by since it borders the forest — keep food well sealed (from reviews)

entries.name: Jungle Garden
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bailan Bay, just past Kai Bae Beach · 5 min walk to the beach
tags: 🌿 Timber bungalows in a quiet garden
entries.addr: 105/7 Moo 1, Haad Bai Lan, Ao Bai Lan, Ko Chang
entries.storyHtml: Jungle Garden is the place for people who come to Koh Chang to "be in nature without paying a fortune" — a cluster of around 12 timber and woven-bamboo bungalows with thatched roofs, spread through a shady green garden in the forest at Bailan Bay on the island's west coast, just south of Kai Bae Beach. · Real reviews keep coming back to three things: a shady, peaceful garden where you wake up to birdsong, a great kitchen at friendly prices, and owners who look after you as warmly as family. · The strongest point people mention is the garden restaurant and bar — many reviews say the food, especially the bold-flavoured Thai dishes, is filling and tasty enough that you barely want to eat out. · Rooms come both as fan bungalows starting at just ฿700 and A/C ones for those who want to sleep more comfortably; every unit has a queen bed, an en-suite bathroom with hot water, and a garden-view balcony. · The thing to understand before booking: this place is not on the beach and has no swimming pool; it's around a 5-minute walk to Bailan Beach, but Bailan itself has little natural sand, so if you want a pretty beach to swim at you'll need to ride to Kai Bae or Klong Prao. · Honest caveats: being in a garden in the forest means the odd ant and insect gets into the room, housekeeping can be inconsistent on some days and needs asking for, and rooms are fairly small for the price. · Best for backpackers, couples and budget travellers who want to stretch their money over more nights, prioritising quiet, nature and good food over luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose an A/C bungalow if you're coming in the hot season or find it hard to sleep, since the more sealed-up room also helps keep insects down. · Bring mosquito repellent and keep food well sealed since you're in a garden in the forest, and rent a motorbike — the Bailan area has few shops and isn't on the beach.
pros: Great kitchen at friendly prices, especially the Thai food (the highlight reviews praise most)
A shady, peaceful garden in the forest where you wake up to birdsong
Owners and family look after you warmly and informally
From just ฿700/night, excellent value among budget bungalows
cons: Not on the beach and no swimming pool — you'll need to ride to a pretty beach to swim
Set in a garden in the forest, so the odd ant and insect gets into the room
Rooms are small for the price · housekeeping is inconsistent on some days (from reviews)

entries.name: Paradise Bungalows
entries.mrtTag: 📍 End of Kai Bae Beach village · 5 min walk to the beach
tags: 🚶 5 min walk to Kai Bae Beach
🌅 Some units get Gulf of Thailand views
entries.addr: 98/8 Moo 4, Kai Bae Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Paradise Bungalows is a down-to-earth, long-running budget stay at the southern end of Kai Bae Beach village — a popular area that sits midway between the buzz of White Sand Beach and the quiet of Lonely Beach. · It's a cluster of around 26 Thai-style timber bungalows stepping up a low hill, with repeat guests who keep coming back, so the feel is warm and island-guesthouse. · The selling point reviews agree on is the central village location, around a 5-minute walk to Kai Bae Beach and within walking distance of restaurants, convenience stores, bars and massage shops everywhere, plus a massage-spa that many reviews single out — some even call it the best they found on Koh Chang — and friendly, helpful staff. · There are several room types, from the cheapest fan bungalows up to large A/C cottages; every unit has a private balcony, and the upper bungalows on the hill get views out over the Gulf of Thailand. · The thing to understand before booking: this place is not on the beach and has no swimming pool; the bungalows sit along a road climbing the hill, around a 5-minute walk down to the beach. · Honest caveats: it's an older property, with furniture and bathrooms in some units worn with age, thin walls that let you hear the next room, weak water pressure in places, and upper bungalows that take a fair climb up the stairs. · Best for backpackers, budget couples and anyone who wants to be in the middle of Kai Bae at a light price, using the stay as a base for getting out and about.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For cool air and a view, ask for 'A/C + upper unit' when you book, since the lower fan rooms are cheaper but can be hot and don't see the sea. · Try booking the on-site massage-spa after a full day out, and if you're travelling with older folks or find stairs hard, ask for a lower unit.
pros: Central Kai Bae village location — easy walk to the beach and restaurants
Massage-spa praised as the best some found on the island · friendly staff
Starting price lighter than many stays in the same area
Bungalows have a private balcony, some with sea views
cons: Not on the beach and no swimming pool · it's an older property
Furniture and bathrooms in some units are worn · thin walls let sound through
Upper bungalows take a fair climb up the stairs (from reviews)

entries.name: Sea Flower Resort
entries.badge: 🌅 Seafront bungalows under a thousand baht
entries.mrtTag: 📍 End of Lonely Beach · 7–10 min walk to the sand
tags: 🌺 Seafront bungalows under a thousand baht
🛋️ Hammocks and bean bags by the water
entries.addr: 4 Moo 1, Ko Chang Tai, Lonely Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among these 9 stays, if you measure by "view per baht," Sea Flower Resort scores very high — a budget seafront bungalow resort at the end of Lonely Beach, running on into Bailan Bay, on the island's southwest side. · What makes it memorable is its clifftop location above the sea with a full-on sunset view, plus a waterside lounging zone set with hammocks, bean bags and chairs to catch the breeze and the last light of the day — which many reviews call the highlight — at room rates starting from just ฿650, under a thousand baht a night. · There are several room types, from the cheapest Economy rooms up to the bungalows and Deluxe Sea View rooms with a balcony and A/C that are the stars here. · The thing to be clear on before booking, which people often get wrong: the front of the resort is sea-facing rocks, not a sandy beach; if you want to swim off the sand you'll need to walk around 7–10 minutes to Lonely Beach, and pack water shoes. · Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no swimming pool and no breakfast automatically included, some of the cheaper rooms are small with little storage, quality varies a lot between room types, and the Lonely Beach zone has bars and beachside parties late at night in high season. · Best for budget travellers, backpackers, and couples who want a romantic seafront bungalow at a light price and value the waterside atmosphere over luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The price gap between a sea-view room and an economy one is small, but you get a balcony to watch the sunset from your door — far better value if you're here for the atmosphere. · Pack water shoes since the front of the stay is rocks, and if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room set further back or away from the bars.
pros: Beautiful clifftop sunset views, a relaxed waterside atmosphere
Sea-view bungalows with a balcony are good value, from just ฿650/night
Hammocks and bean bags by the water — a chill corner many reviews call the highlight
Easy walk to Lonely Beach restaurants and bars · easygoing staff
cons: The front of the resort is rocks, not a sandy beach — 7–10 min walk to the beach
No swimming pool · no breakfast automatically included
Some cheaper rooms are small, quality varies by type (from reviews)

entries.name: Elephant Bay Resort
entries.badge: 🏊 Big bayside pool · most reviews in the set
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bailan Bay · 15 min walk to the sand (Lonely Beach)
entries.addr: 6/17 Moo 1, Bailan Bay, Ko Chang Tai, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among these 9 stays, if you measure by review count, Elephant Bay Resort is the one with the most — over 502 reviews on Booking.com at a score of 8.2 (Agoda 8.3). · It's a compact pool resort of around 26 rooms hidden along Bailan Bay on the island's southwest side, leaning on "good value and friendly" more than luxury. · The thing reviews mention most is the large outdoor swimming pool at the heart of the resort, ringed by a wide green garden and sun loungers, paired with a bright-toned sea-view bar and restaurant, a billiards table, and a garden for light sports. · Rooms are bungalows and low concrete buildings in bright tones, both fan and A/C (A/C rooms are limited), most with a private balcony; many reviews say the rooms are bigger and cleaner than expected at this price. · The thing to understand before booking: the front of the resort is a rocky waterfront, not a sandy beach to swim off, so the pool is the main place to swim — if you want the sea, walk or take a songthaew to White Sand Beach (Lonely Beach), around 15 minutes. · Honest caveats: some rooms are plain or starting to age, the beds are fairly firm, views from some rooms are of the garden rather than the sea, and Wi-Fi in some of the deeper-set bungalows is unstable. · Best for backpackers, couples, groups of friends and families who prioritise value, want to stay along a quiet bay with a pool to soak in, at a price where finding a resort with a pool like this isn't easy.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The front of the resort is rocks — if you want to swim in the sea, walk or take a songthaew to White Sand Beach (Lonely Beach), around 15 minutes, ideally in the evening for the sunset. · A/C rooms are limited, so if you want A/C, specify it and book ahead, and if you need to work online, ask for a room near the pool or reception.
pros: Big swimming pool and wide garden at a budget price — great value
Most reviews in the set at 502 · score 8.2 · friendly service
Rooms bigger and cleaner than expected, good bathrooms, cool A/C
Quiet bayside atmosphere, walkable to White Sand Beach, good for families
cons: The front of the resort is rocks, not a sandy beach to swim off
Some rooms are plain or starting to age, beds are fairly firm
Wi-Fi in some of the deeper-set bungalows is unstable (from reviews)

entries.type: Budget Hotel on the Main Road 2★
entries.name: Kachapol Hotel
entries.badge: 💸 Clean rooms · best value in Klong Prao
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Prao Beach, on the main road · 4–5 min walk to the beach
tags: 💸 Light price, best value in the area
entries.addr: 34/8 Moo 4, Klong Prao, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Kachapol Hotel is a budget hotel for people who come to Koh Chang to "get out and explore" rather than soak in a resort all day — a small hotel of around 20 rooms sitting right on the main road in the Klong Prao Beach area on the island's west coast, near the edge of Kai Bae. · This is a no-frills stay selling the value of a clean bedroom in a good location. · The thing real reviews most agree on praising is that the A/C rooms are clearly bigger and cleaner than the price you pay — many say they're bigger than hotels at the same price in other areas (one foreign review suggests asking for "room B12" because it's especially large) — plus a location that's around a 4–5 minute walk to Klong Prao Beach, with restaurants, convenience stores and motorbike rental shops lined up nearby, and free private parking. · A note on the name: the hotel was once called OYO 918 Kachapol Hotel while it was in the OYO chain and has gone back to Kachapol Hotel — it's the same place. · The thing to understand before booking: this is not a beachfront resort, has no swimming pool, and doesn't include breakfast. · Honest caveats: because it's on the main road with fairly thin walls between rooms, the roadside rooms get traffic noise and sound from next door, some staff have limited English, and in low season the Wi-Fi/some services may not be at full strength — which is why it's the lowest-scoring in the set at 7.2. · Best for budget travellers, backpackers and people riding a motorbike around the island who just want a clean room to sleep in after a full day out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room at the back or interior of the building if you're a light sleeper, since the roadside rooms get traffic noise and the walls are fairly thin. · Rent a motorbike (there's free parking) to get the most out of this location, and plan breakfast at the rice-soup, congee and coffee spots nearby since there's no breakfast at the hotel.
pros: Rooms bigger and cleaner than the price you pay, better than expected on this budget
Good location — easy walk to Klong Prao Beach and restaurants
Free private parking, handy for those renting a car/motorbike
Very light price from ฿700/night, best value in the Klong Prao area
cons: Thin walls and on the main road — you hear the next room and traffic
No swimming pool and no breakfast included · budget-hotel level of service
Some staff have limited English (from reviews)

entries.name: Kohchang7 Guest House
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bailan Bay, on the rocks · ~10 min drive from Kai Bae Beach
tags: 🌅 Sea and sunset views on the rocks
entries.addr: 6/2 Moo 1, Bailan Bay, Ko Chang Tai, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among these 9 stays, if you go by starting price, Kohchang7 Guest House (some platforms list it as Kohchang7 Seaview Bungalow) is the cheapest, from just ฿550/night — a small guesthouse of around 20 rooms clinging to the rocks above the sea in Bailan Bay on the island's west coast, a quiet bay between Kai Bae Beach and Lonely Beach. · The straightforward selling points reviews mention are sea views, a beautiful sunset, peace and quiet away from the crowds, and a praised Thai-Korean kitchen, all at a very light price. · Another highlight is its seafront location where you can go snorkelling straight off the front of the stay, via steps and the rocks, with the guesthouse lending snorkelling gear for free. · Rooms range from budget fan bungalows to sea-view A/C rooms and front-row seafront bungalows whose balconies face straight out to sea, which reviews say get the full sunset. · The thing to understand before booking: this place is not a sandy beach; you get into the water via the rocks and steps, better for snorkelling than walking the sand, and there's no swimming pool. · Honest caveats: some rooms look old and upkeep is inconsistent, water pressure is weak with an iron smell to the water at times, the cheaper rooms often have no TV/fridge, and the location is remote with a narrow, steep access road and no convenience store nearby. · Best for couples and backpackers who want a seafront location, sunset views, quiet and good food at the lightest price in the set.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The selling point is the sunset, so ask for a sea-view A/C room or a front-row bungalow whose balcony faces out to sea when you book. · The access road is narrow and steep with no convenience store nearby, so if you're not driving, arrange a transfer in advance or rent a motorbike, and bring mosquito repellent, a torch and rubber shoes for walking the rocks.
pros: Seafront location, beautiful sunset views, peaceful and away from the crowds
Snorkel straight off the front of the stay, with gear to borrow for free
Tasty Thai-Korean kitchen, friendly English-speaking owners
Cheapest in the set, from just ฿550/night, good value for a seafront stay
cons: Not a sandy beach — you get in via the rocks and steps · no pool
Some rooms look old, water pressure is weak with a smell at times
Remote location, narrow steep access road, no convenience store nearby (from reviews)

entries.name: Cliff Cottage
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Bao, on the cliff · Klong Kloi Beach ~10 min walk
entries.addr: 108 Moo 1, Bang Bao, Ko Chang Tai, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Cliff Cottage is a small eco-resort clinging to the cliff above Bang Bao bay at the far south of Koh Chang, in an old fishing-village area that still keeps its original feel — for people who want to escape the bustle of White Sand Beach and be with nature and the real sea. · The selling point reviews agree on is sunset views over the sea that many say never disappoint, peace and quiet away from the crowds, and a standout you won't find at similarly priced stays — an in-house PADI 5-Star BBdivers dive centre offering dive courses, scuba, snorkelling and free-diving, plus free kayaking and snorkelling from in front of the restaurant. · There are several room types, from the budget Castaway rooms (fan/shared bathroom) and the en-suite A/C Garden Room up to the Cliff Top Bungalow on the cliff with sea views that reviews talk about most, plus glamping tents open only in the dry season. · The clifftop restaurant serves Thai-Western food, praised for taste and open nearly all day. · The thing to understand before booking: this place is not a sandy beachfront stay; it's a cliff above a rocky bay, with only a small splash pool to soak in, and the nearest sandy beach is Klong Kloi, around a 10-minute walk. · Honest caveats: rooms are basic and fairly small, especially the Castaway rooms, cleanliness is inconsistent at times, there are water issues during the island's dry spells (an island-wide problem in some seasons), and getting around the island is fairly limited. · Best for divers, couples, and anyone who wants sunset views and quiet out in nature on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Not every room gets the same view — specify a Cliff Top Bungalow or a room facing out to the western sea when you book. · Make the most of the in-house BBdivers dive centre and borrow the kayak/snorkel for free. · The resort is on the cliff around 1.5 km from the village — renting a motorbike or asking about a pier transfer in advance is recommended.
pros: Beautiful views over Bang Bao bay and sunsets that never disappoint (from reviews)
In-house PADI BBdivers dive centre + free kayak/snorkel out front
Tasty, good-value clifftop restaurant open nearly all day · kind staff
Eco, quiet, from just ฿700/night, pet-friendly
cons: Not on a sandy beach — only a small pool to soak in, you walk to Klong Kloi Beach
Rooms are basic and fairly small, especially the Castaway rooms
Cleanliness is inconsistent at times · water issues during the island's dry spells

adviceTitle: How to pick the right budget stay on Koh Chang for your trip?

advice.head: Want a quiet garden, a pool, the highest score
advice.bodyHtml: → Macura Resort ฿700, a boutique resort in a garden with a saltwater pool, owner-run, score 9.0 — highest in the set (~5 min drive to White Sand Beach)

advice.head: Want a stay with character and great atmosphere
advice.bodyHtml: → Oasis Koh Chang ฿900, hillside bungalows with a treehouse restaurant and an infinity pool with forest-sea views — a popular sunset spot

advice.head: Tightest budget, focused on good food and quiet
advice.bodyHtml: → Jungle Garden ฿700, timber bungalows in a garden with a great kitchen, or Kohchang7 ฿550 (cheapest), a seafront sunset guesthouse

advice.head: Want a swimming pool on a budget
advice.bodyHtml: → Elephant Bay Resort ฿900, a big pool by Bailan Bay, a wide garden, the most reviews at 502 — good for groups and families

advice.head: Want a seafront bungalow with sunset views
advice.bodyHtml: → Sea Flower Resort ฿650, clifftop sunset-view bungalows with hammocks by the water, or Kohchang7 ฿550, on the rocks at Bailan Bay

advice.head: Here to dive, to be out in quiet nature
advice.bodyHtml: → Cliff Cottage ฿700, a clifftop eco-resort at Bang Bao with an in-house PADI BBdivers dive centre, free kayak/snorkel out front

advice.head: Want a central location, a walk to the beach, best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Paradise Bungalows ฿850, central Kai Bae with a good massage-spa · or Kachapol Hotel ฿700, clean rooms in Klong Prao, 4–5 min walk to the beach

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates based on the entry-level room ranges and may change by date and season — always check the real price and compare 3 sites before booking. · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. · One thing to understand together is that most budget stays on Koh Chang are not on the sand — they're usually set in gardens, up on the hills, or along the rocks, with a walk or a ride to the beach. · Kachapol Hotel was once called OYO 918 Kachapol — it's the same place. · In high season (Nov–Apr) prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book ahead and choose free cancellation first. · In the monsoon (May–Oct) Koh Chang gets rain and wind, and some small stays cut services or close for part of the time, so check before booking and check the ferry schedule. · Getting around the island is fairly limited — renting a motorbike is recommended. · Article by Thailandaddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about budget stays on Koh Chang

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best budget stay on Koh Chang?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. · By score, Macura Resort is highest in the set at 9.0, a boutique resort in a garden with a saltwater pool. · By review count and if you want a pool, Elephant Bay Resort has the most reviews at 502, with a big bayside pool. · For a stay with character, Oasis has a treehouse restaurant and an infinity pool. · For seafront and sunset views, Sea Flower or Kohchang7. · For diving, Cliff Cottage has its own dive centre.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays on Koh Chang cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at around ฿550–900 per night for entry-level rooms. · The cheapest is Kohchang7 from ฿550, then Sea Flower at ฿650. · Most of the rest start around ฿700–900 (Macura, Jungle Garden, Cliff Cottage, Kachapol ฿700 · Paradise ฿850 · Oasis, Elephant Bay ฿900). · A/C rooms or sea-view bungalows climb to around ฿1,000–1,900. · In high season and over long holidays, prices rise and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ Are budget stays on Koh Chang on the beach?
faq.a: Most are not on the sand, which is an important thing to understand before booking. · Macura, Jungle Garden and Kachapol are garden/roadside stays, a 5-minute walk or drive to the beach. · Oasis and Paradise are on the hill, walking down to the beach. · Sea Flower, Elephant Bay and Kohchang7 are seafront, but the front of the stay is rocks, not sand. · Cliff Cottage is on the cliff. · If you want to walk from your room straight onto the sand, budget stays on Koh Chang barely exist for that — you'd need to move up to a beachfront resort.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in for a budget stay on Koh Chang?
faq.a: White Sand Beach is lively with lots of shops (Macura is near it) · Klong Prao–Kai Bae is mid-island, handy, with a swimmable beach and lovely sunsets (Paradise, Kachapol) · Bailan Bay is a small, quiet bay on the rocks, good for snorkelling (Jungle Garden, Elephant Bay, Kohchang7) · Lonely Beach is the backpacker and beach-bar crowd (Oasis, Sea Flower) · Bang Bao is at the far south, quiet, good for divers (Cliff Cottage).

faq.q: ❓ Which budget stays on Koh Chang have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There are 3 in this set with a pool. · Elephant Bay Resort has a large outdoor pool at the heart of the resort. · Macura Resort has a saltwater pool, easy to swim in without stinging your eyes. · Oasis Koh Chang has an infinity pool with forest-sea views. · Cliff Cottage has only a small splash pool to soak in. · The rest (Jungle Garden, Paradise, Sea Flower, Kachapol, Kohchang7) have no swimming pool — you swim at the beach or the sea.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Koh Chang stay · can I go in the monsoon?
faq.a: Most stays in this article are small (12–26 rooms) and fill fast. · In high season (November–April) and over long holidays, book 2–4 weeks ahead or more. · In the monsoon (May–October), Koh Chang gets rain and wind, prices drop and it's very quiet, but some small stays cut services or close for part of the time, and Cliff Cottage's glamping tents open only in the dry season, so check directly with the stay before booking and check the ferry schedule. · Every platform offers free cancellation — locking in a rate like that first is recommended if your plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
